Final categorization: POSSIBLE  
(Justification: This is a non-review original research paper that uses future vegetation productivity projections—derived from Dynamic Habitat Index (DHI) metrics under IPCC climate scenarios—as input data to inform conservation prioritization in Canada’s boreal forest. While the study operates at a national scale (entire Canadian boreal zone), implements multiple future climate scenarios (B1, A1B, A2), and includes spatially explicit modeling, its primary objective is not land use/land cover (LULC) prediction. Instead, LULC-related vegetation productivity variability (VVP) is used as an input layer in a conservation planning framework (Marxan/MarProb). The actual LULC or vegetation productivity projections were produced in a prior study (Nelson et al. 2014), and this paper does not develop or validate those predictions nor report accuracy metrics for them. Thus, LULC prediction is incidental—not the central focus—and serves as a supporting input for systematic conservation planning. The paper meets none of the exclusion criteria but fails the core inclusion criterion that “Primary focus = LULC prediction.” Therefore, it is categorized as 'POSSIBLE'.)
